headline: The 10-year yield eased to 5.19% and Brent slipped below $105, letting spot buyers drive a rebound; but ETFs bled another $65.4M on Monday and weighted funding sits at just 2.67% annualized as the market waits flat for tonight's CPI.
summary: The market stage remains bull (since 10/09; 34 straight closes above a rising 200-day average), and no exit-framework rule has fired or is close. Tuesday's bounce was spot-led as macro pressure eased, but ETFs are still seeing outflows, leverage has not returned and the share of short-term holders in profit fell to 68%, so this is consolidation rather than renewed strength. Next: core CPI for September at 20:30 Taipei on 10/14 (12:30 UTC), and the orders and supply clusters between 82,000 and 84,000.

overview.lead: Day 5 of the bull stage: Tuesday recovered about half the drop without new money following, valuation is still mid-cycle, and all three views say hold, no action.
points: Market stage: bull (since 10/09), 34 straight closes above a rising 200-day average.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak 0.547 (last edition 0.560), still 34.9% from the on-chain sell line (CoinMetrics 10/12).
Power-law multiple 0.572 (10/12): above the historical bottom band of 0.24–0.48 and below fair value of 143,037.
Tidemark top signal 0, bottom signal 22.5 — no signal either way (price date 10/12, not stale).

cycle.lead: Market stage: bull (since 2026-10-09); 34 straight closes above a rising 200-day average (threshold 30).
points: The 200-day average is 72,128, above 70,137 thirty days ago and still rising; capitulation has occurred (2026-06-30, 58,525).

Evidence lights 3/5 (strength of evidence only, not part of the rule): MVRV above its 1-year mean (1.519 vs 1.441), realized cap +1.26% over 30 days, and close above the short-term holder cost basis of 74,327 (10/07) are lit; 12-month momentum (−29.0%) and 90-day exchange supply (+0.50%) are not.
By rule, a return from bull to bear needs 30 straight closes below a falling 200-day average; days below: 0.
Tidemark low test: no break of 58,525 before 12/19; long-term path weights 30/20/25/25, next review 10/31.

market.lead: Tuesday bounced from near the 50-day average back into the value area but stayed under the 20-day average — short-term range trading.
points: Intraday 80,951–84,053, closing at 69.3% of the day's range; volume 1.22× the 20-day average and 1.22× the prior day; VWAP 83,096.
Value area 82,500–85,500 with point of control 84,000; the close is back inside the value area; 20-day range position 29.4% (last edition 1.1%).
The 20-day average of 83,942 is about 1.0% above, the 50-day average of 81,103 is 2.4% below; Mayer multiple 1.152.
The up-leg from 6/30 has run 105 days and +42.0%, −4.0% from its high of 86,594; the leg-end line of 73,605 is 11.4% below (reading only).

deriv.lead: No leverage behind the bounce: funding diverges across venues and the weighted rate is near zero, while demand for protection edged up — leverage stays light.
points: Three-venue weighted funding 2.67% annualized (last edition −0.12%); Hyperliquid 7.88%, OKX −3.36%, Deribit 0.44% — mixed direction.
30-day 25Δ risk reversal −2.98 (last edition −2.42), puts 38.49 vs calls 35.51; DVOL 38.23, 25.8th percentile of the year.
The 10/16 weekly expiry has max pain at 83,000 and 4.3% of OI; 10/30 holds 37.5% with max pain 79,000; 12/25 holds 33.0% with max pain 75,000.

Order book (10/14 00:06 UTC, mid 83,179): within ±10%, bids $822M vs asks $581M; Hyperliquid perp has a ~$234M ask wall at 83,000 and a ~$193M bid wall at 82,000, with near-book sides roughly even (orders can be pulled; reading only).

flows.lead: Macro pressure eased for now, but ETFs have not resumed inflows and US buying is soft — flows are neutral to weak, while new capital is still trickling in.
points: Latest complete ETF day 10/09: +$21.1M (The Block); the seven trading days 10/01–10/09 total −$388.6M; 10/12 provisional −$65.4M (Farside and SoSoValue agree, all from IBIT); 10/13 not available today.
US 10-year yield 5.24%, real yield 2.91%, up 31 bp over 20 observations (FRED 10/09); intraday 10/13 it eased to about 5.19% (Kitco).
Realized cap +1.26% over 30 days (10/12): capital is still flowing in; stablecoin supply $311.1B, +0.78% over 30 days.
Coinbase premium −0.081% (7-day avg −0.094%), soft US demand; Fear & Greed 57 (73 a week ago); BTC–Nasdaq 30-day correlation 0.678 (10/12).

onchain.lead: Monday's drop cut the share of short-term holders in profit sharply and long-term holder selling rose slightly, but exchange supply did not grow — the structure is intact.
points: Short-term holders in profit 68.18% (10/12, last edition 83.02%); their cost basis of 74,327 (10/07) sits about 10.6% below price.
Long-term holders net −78.2K BTC over 30 days (10/12, last edition −62.1K); exchange supply +0.01% over 7 days, −1.32% over 30, +0.50% over 90.
The 82–84K bucket at price holds 747K BTC; 84–86K above holds 1.261M BTC of overhead supply; 76–78K below holds 557K BTC (URPD 10/12).

Large holders (100–1K) +27.4K BTC over 30 days and +107.0K since the leg began; 1K–10K +37.9K over 30 days but −28.4K over 7; hash ribbons show no capitulation (48 days), difficulty est. +5.45% (10/16).

exit.lead: Zero exit-framework rules fired today and none are close; all three top indicators are below 60.
points: Price ladder from 125K, 12.5% per step, 8 steps; step 1 is still 50.4% away.
On-chain MVRV ratio 0.547, 0.75/0.80 streaks both 0; top-three percentiles MVRV Z 41.5 / NUPL 41.2 / Puell 57.1 (10/12) — any two must reach 80 to enter the top zone.
200-day hedge streak 0, distance −13.2%; it fires after 5 straight closes below 72,128, cutting 20%.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs saw −$65.4M on 10/12, all from BlackRock's IBIT with zero flow elsewhere; total assets about $106B
news.read: Farside also shows −$65.4M, entered on site as the 10/12 provisional value. Far smaller than −$487.1M on 10/07: outflows slowing, not reversing; including 10/12 the last 7 trading days total about −$557M. ETFs are this cycle's main marginal buyer, so while they bleed the 1.26M BTC of overhead supply at 84–86K is harder to absorb; but realized cap is still +1.26% over 30 days. No change to the market stage or exit framework.

news.title: US September CPI due tonight: headline seen +0.6% m/m and 3.6% y/y (from 3.4%), core about +0.2% m/m; October hike odds about 23%
news.read: Energy lifting the headline is consensus; core is the swing factor: a hot core revives 10/28 hike bets and lifts yields, a soft one cements a hold. With a 0.678 BTC–Nasdaq 30-day correlation, CPI will move BTC short term via yields and stocks, but it won't change the market stage (watch the 200-day average, −13.2% away) or on-chain valuation.

news.title: The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 5.19% (last week's high 5.365%), the dollar index fell to 102.3 from its highest since April 2025, and Brent dropped about 2% to $104.6
news.read: Yields and oil, which weighed on BTC last edition, eased together — the macro backdrop for Tuesday's bounce. The site's FRED reading is still 5.24% for 10/09 with a 2.91% real yield (+31 bp over 20 days); the high-rate regime is unchanged. Short-term relief; whether it lasts depends on CPI.

news.title: A wallet held since March 2020 moved about 4,582 BTC (~$378M) on Monday to five new addresses, which have not moved since
news.read: Same direction as the site's long-term holders at −78.2K BTC over 30 days (last edition −62.1K), but so far this is a wallet-to-wallet move with no sign of reaching exchanges; exchange supply is +0.01% over 7 days. A single event that doesn't change the cycle view.

news.title: Strive bought 3,311 BTC last week to hold 32,773 BTC, and plans a $500M offering of new 15%-dividend perpetual preferred SATS to buy more
news.read: Corporate treasuries are still buying, but a 15% dividend shows funding is expensive; the size is modest next to ETF outflows in the hundreds of millions per week. For reference; no framework condition changes.

news.title: Metaplanet plans about $328.5M of zero-coupon yen convertibles, ~$149.4M to repay BTC-backed loans; those loans are 17.7% of its BTC NAV vs a 10% guideline
news.read: Refinancing to cut coin-collateralized leverage lowers forced-selling risk; no new buying is involved. No measurable effect on site data.

news.title: South Korea's KOSPI fell about 5.5% Tuesday and SK Hynix about 10%, while BTC closed higher; their 20-period rolling correlation is −0.41
news.read: BTC didn't follow Asian tech lower on AI worries, but its 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq is still 0.678 — US equities remain the main link. Correlation isn't proof of rotation; a short-term reading.

news.title: A London High Court ruling that Chinese law governs victims' claims in the Qian Zhimin case raises the UK government's chances of keeping ~61,000 seized BTC (~$5B); victims will appeal
news.read: Ownership is unresolved and no sale plan was reported; only a future government disposal would create potential supply. No near-term effect on site exchange supply or flows.

news.title: Russia's central bank added Sberbank, the country's largest bank, to its crypto exchange register (9 firms); BTC and other trading opens to all clients around 12/01
news.read: A major bank channel opening is long-term adoption progress, but it starts in December at unknown scale; no effect on any site indicator.

actions.text: Both nearest action points are far: the 200-day average at 72,128 below (−13.2%) and the MVRV 0.75 line at 112,099 above (+34.9%).

actions.head: Don't chase a one-day spot bounce as a trend change, and don't add leverage to bet on CPI.
actions.text: ETFs are still bleeding, weighted funding is just 2.67% and the risk reversal is −2.98 — no flow or leverage confirmation; the close is still below the 20-day average of 83,942.

actions.text: Also watch today's 10/13 ETF flow print and whether the 10-year yield holds near or below 5.2%.

changes.title: High-volume rebound back into the value area; 20-day range position recovers
changes.say: Recovered about 70% of Monday's drop but still below the 20-day average; the 200-day distance widened from −11.9% to −13.2%, moving the hedge condition further away.

changes.title: Complete ETF data advanced to 10/09; 10/12 provisional shows another outflow
changes.say: Outflows are shrinking but haven't reversed; flows remain the bounce's biggest gap, not a framework condition.

changes.title: Funding flipped positive, but Deribit dropped to near zero
changes.say: Venues diverge and leverage overall stays light; risk reversal −2.42 → −2.98, protection demand hasn't faded.

changes.title: Share of short-term holders in profit fell sharply; long-term holder selling rose slightly
changes.say: Monday's drop squeezed recent buyers' profits, but their 74,327 cost basis is still 10.6% below price and exchange supply didn't rise — structure unchanged.

changes.title: All three top indicators eased
changes.say: Further from the 80 top-zone threshold; no framework condition changes.

research.summary: No new Glassnode issue (latest Market Pulse Week 42 on 10/12, The Week On-chain on 10/07); its view that perp traders and ETF holders sold while new capital kept arriving matches the site's ETF outflows, low funding and +1.26% 30-day realized cap; K33's new 10/12 note was preview-only; no new weekly from The Block Research or Coinbase Institutional in the past 7 days.

items.title: Chopping lower
items.points: (Preview only) BTC fell from 86,000 to below 80,500 in a week and now consolidates at 80,000–84,000; spot volume at a one-month low, open interest stagnant; correlation with US equities at a four-month high.
items.meaning: Paywalled, not used as a basis for judgment; the preview agrees with the site's light leverage and 0.678 Nasdaq 30-day correlation.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 42
items.points: Thursday's break below 81K returned BTC to the breakout point of three weeks ago, weekly close down about 3%; weekly ETF flows +$118M → −$702M; perp CVD down to −$682M; 25Δ skew 2.1% → 4.46%; supply in profit 74.5% → 71.4%; monthly realized-cap change +1.2%.
items.meaning: Consistent with the site: risk reversal −2.98, ETF outflows, realized cap still growing. Its weekly ETF figure uses a different basis from the site's; not subtracted. Short-term structure; no change to the market stage or exit framework.

items.title: The Week On-chain: A Rally Running Light
items.points: Ask wall at 86.5K–86.75K, largest bid wall at 81K–81.25K; reclaiming 85.5K is needed for recovery; ~$4.9B of new capital over 30 days vs a $12.8B realized-cap rise; long liquidation band 81.7K–83.3K, then 75K.
items.meaning: Tuesday's low of 80,951 held near its 81K bid wall before bouncing; until 85.5K is reclaimed it's consolidation, consistent with the site's close below the 20-day average and the 85,500 value-area top.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 41
items.points: BTC near 86K, weekly close up about 2%; derivatives positioning normalized; ETF inflows cooled; on-chain activity strengthened.
items.meaning: Its call on cooling ETF inflows was confirmed by two weeks of outflows since; consistent with the site.
